subject: biochemistry
title: Minerals and trace elements: iron, copper, zinc, selenium and iodine

steps.tx: Dietary ferric iron (Fe3+) is reduced to ferrous iron (Fe2+) by duodenal **cytochrome b (Dcytb)** and absorbed via divalent metal transporter 1 (DMT1). Basolateral export into circulation requires **ferroportin** coupled to oxidation by hephaestin. Circulating iron binds **transferrin**, while intracellular iron is stored within **ferritin**. The liver secretes **hepcidin** in response to high iron stores or systemic inflammation. Hepcidin binds ferroportin, inducing its endocytosis and degradation, thereby locking iron inside enterocytes and macrophages.
steps.say: Non-heme iron is reduced in the duodenum and transported into enterocytes by DMT1. Ferroportin exports iron into blood, where transferrin carries it. Hepcidin from the liver degrades ferroportin during inflammation or iron excess, blocking iron release and causing anaemia of chronic disease.

nodes.label: Dietary Fe3+ reduced to Fe2+ by Dcytb
Apical uptake via DMT1 into enterocyte
Basolateral export via Ferroportin and Hephaestin
Serum transport by Transferrin to tissues

steps.tx: **Hereditary haemochromatosis** is an autosomal recessive disorder most commonly caused by **HFE gene mutations (C282Y/H63D)**. Defective HFE signaling suppresses hepcidin synthesis, causing uncontrolled intestinal iron absorption and systemic overload. Excess iron catalyzes Fenton reactions, generating hydroxyl free radicals that damage organs. The classic clinical tetrad includes **bronze diabetes** (hyperpigmentation and diabetes mellitus), micronodular cirrhosis, pseudogout, and dilated cardiomyopathy. Therapeutic phlebotomy prevents irreversible end-organ fibrosis.
steps.say: Hereditary haemochromatosis results from HFE mutations that decrease hepcidin production, causing unchecked iron absorption. Free iron damages parenchymal cells via free radicals, leading to bronze skin pigmentation, diabetes, cirrhosis, cardiomyopathy, and arthropathy. Phlebotomy is life saving.

rows: Iron deposition in hepatocytes and Kupffer cells
Cirrhosis, markedly increased risk of hepatocellular carcinoma
Deposition in beta cells causing cell loss
Melanin and hemosiderin accumulation in dermis
Deposition in myocardium and conducting system
Chondrocalcinosis, pseudogout in second and third MCP joints

steps.tx: Absorbed copper travels to hepatocytes and incorporates into **ceruloplasmin** via the copper-transporting P-type ATPase **ATP7B**. Excess copper is excreted into bile through ATP7B. Mutations in ATP7B cause **Wilson disease (hepatolenticular degeneration)**. Copper fails to enter ceruloplasmin or bile, accumulating in hepatocytes and eventually spilling into blood to deposit in basal ganglia, cornea, and kidneys. Hallmarks include cirrhosis, parkinsonian movement disorders, psychiatric changes, low ceruloplasmin, and **Kayser-Fleischer rings**.
steps.say: ATP7B coordinates copper incorporation into ceruloplasmin and excretion into bile. Mutated ATP7B in Wilson disease causes toxic copper accumulation in liver, brain, and cornea. Patients develop cirrhosis, tremor, psychiatric illness, Kayser-Fleischer rings, and low serum ceruloplasmin.

nodes.label: Impaired biliary excretion and ceruloplasmin loading
Low serum ceruloplasmin, free copper toxic release
Deposition in liver, lenticular nuclei, Descemet membrane

steps.tx: **Zinc** functions as an essential cofactor for over 300 metalloenzymes including carbonic anhydrase, alkaline phosphatase, RNA polymerase, and zinc-finger transcription factors. **Acrodermatitis enteropathica** is an inherited zinc malabsorption disorder presenting with periorificial and acral vesiculobullous dermatitis, alopecia, and chronic diarrhoea. **Selenium** incorporates as selenocysteine into **glutathione peroxidase**, protecting against lipid peroxidation. Severe selenium deficiency causes **Keshan disease**, an endemic congestive cardiomyopathy seen in selenium-deficient geographical regions.
steps.say: Zinc is required for hundreds of enzymes and zinc-finger motifs. Inherited zinc malabsorption causes acrodermatitis enteropathica with periorificial pustular rashes, alopecia, and diarrhoea. Selenium is vital for glutathione peroxidase; deficiency causes Keshan disease cardiomyopathy.

left.title: Zinc Deficiency
points: Impaired cellular immunity and recurrent infections

right.title: Selenium Deficiency
points: Enhanced susceptibility to oxidative tissue injury

steps.tx: Thyroid follicular cells trap circulating iodide via the **sodium-iodide symporter (NIS)**. **Thyroperoxidase (TPO)** oxidizes iodide to iodine and catalyzes the iodination of tyrosine residues on thyroglobulin (**organification**), generating monoiodotyrosine (MIT) and diiodotyrosine (DIT). TPO couples MIT and DIT to form triiodothyronine (T3) and thyroxine (T4). Severe dietary iodine deficiency causes compensatory goitre from chronic TSH stimulation, and untreated maternal deficiency leads to endemic **congenital cretinism** with profound cognitive impairment and short stature.
steps.say: Iodide is concentrated into thyroid follicular cells by the sodium-iodide symporter. Thyroid peroxidase oxidizes iodide and iodinates thyroglobulin to create T3 and T4. Severe dietary iodine deficiency causes goitre, and in pregnant women causes congenital cretinism in the newborn.

nodes.label: Iodide uptake via basolateral Na+/I- symporter
Pendrin apical transport into follicular lumen
Organification to form MIT and DIT residues on thyroglobulin
Coupling generates T3 and T4 for endocytosis and secretion
